name: Hebrew
description: Eber@Gen.10.21-Luk   עֵבֶר (Eber, H5677)   People from Eber@Gen.10.21-Luk

points: Because Lot dwelt in Sodom he was carried away captive with his goods, and one that escaped told Abram the Hebrew.

note.label: Genesis 14: The War of the Kings and Melchizedek

points: The king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah: when ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, if it be a son, then ye shall kill him. Pharaoh commanded the male children killed at birth. That is oppression, and America does the same thing.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

points: Pharaoh told the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah the most notable, that when they saw the women on the stools and it was a son they were to kill him; women then birthed sitting, with gravity, and the baby came fast.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: The midwives feared God and did not; their answer, the Hebrew women are lively and delivered ere the midwives come, means our women had birthed before they arrived and a living child could not be killed.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: The midwives answered Pharaoh that the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women, for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them; the daughters of Israel are not as the women of the nations.

note.label: Exodus 1: A New King Over Egypt Which Knew Not Joseph

points: She knew the child was a Hebrew and no Egyptian because the Most High put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel; though both peoples were dark of skin, this was a child of the chosen nation.
Miriam was crafty. She offered to call a nurse of the Hebrew women, and Pharaoh's daughter sent the maid, who called the child's own mother, and wages were paid her to nurse him.

Moses went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren; and he slew the Egyptian. Some of you might say Moses was a murderer; he did not kill out of hatred. What Moses did is the spirit the brothers had in the time of the Black Panthers, when racist police were killing our people; there are men locked up right now as prisoners of war from that era. We do not do that today, but that is the spirit Moses was moving in.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

points: When Moses was grown he went out unto his brethren the Israelites and looked on their burdens, and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. Moses knew the Israelites were his brothers; he knew he was not of the Egyptian lineage and that there was something different about him.

If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he came in by himself he goes out by himself; if he were married when he came in, his wife goes out with him.

Deuteronomy repeats the same judgment for a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman sold unto thee. Nehemiah 5 shows how brethren came into servitude: in the dearth some mortgaged lands, vineyards, and houses to buy corn, some borrowed money for the king's tribute, and some brought their sons and daughters into bondage. The brother that waxes poor is not to be compelled to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant, and not ruled over harshly.
Zedekiah's covenant in Jeremiah confirms the law in the prophets: every man was to let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release.

note.label: Exodus 21: The Judgments Set Before Israel

points: If thy brother, an Hebrew man or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee and serve thee six years, then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free, and thou shalt not let him go away empty.

note.label: Deuteronomy 15: The Year of Release and the Hebrew Servant

points: Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people at Jerusalem to proclaim liberty, that every man let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free and none serve himself of his Jewish brother.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

points: The Most High reminds them He made a covenant with their fathers when He brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, that at the end of seven years every man should let his Hebrew brother go free.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

points: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.
